title: Unsafe tool access
content: An agent should only invoke tools explicitly permitted by its authorization policy. Tool availability alone must not grant unrestricted access.

title: Permission validation
content: Every sensitive tool request should be checked against the current user or agent permissions before execution.

title: Instruction boundary
content: Untrusted content should not override higher-priority system instructions or authorization constraints.

title: Memory validation
content: Information written to agent memory should be validated and should not automatically be treated as trusted instructions.

title: Least privilege
content: Agent tools should operate with the minimum permissions required for their intended task.

title: Deterministic testing
content: Security tests in a research sandbox should be deterministic and repeatable so findings can be reproduced.

title: Finding dependencies
content: A previous finding can be used to prioritize a permitted test that examines a related weakness, but the test must remain within the sandbox allowlist.

title: Evidence-based findings
content: A potential vulnerability should be supported by evidence produced by the controlled sandbox and should not be treated as validated without reproduction.

title: Access control
content: Authorization checks should occur before an agent performs an operation that requires elevated or restricted permissions.

title: Authorization failure handling
content: When an authorization check fails, the restricted operation should not be executed and the failure should be recorded as evidence.

title: Agent permission boundaries
content: An agent's available capabilities should be limited to the permissions required for its defined task and execution context.

title: Tool exposure
content: A tool being registered or exposed to an agent does not by itself establish that the agent is authorized to use it.

title: Sensitive tool authorization
content: Tools that can access sensitive resources should verify authorization for each relevant request rather than relying only on tool availability.

title: Untrusted memory content
content: Data retrieved from memory should be treated according to its trust level and should not automatically become an instruction for the agent.

title: Memory integrity
content: Agent memory should have validation boundaries that prevent untrusted or malformed information from being accepted as trusted state.

title: Untrusted instructions
content: Instructions originating from untrusted content should be distinguished from trusted system or application instructions.

title: Authorization protection
content: Prompt content should not be allowed to bypass authorization rules or cause the agent to perform an operation outside its permitted capabilities.

title: Adaptive test selection
content: Adaptive security testing can use previous findings and test results to select the next permitted test in the controlled chain.

title: Test dependencies
content: A dependent security test should only be considered after its required prerequisite tests have completed successfully.

title: Controlled sandbox testing
content: Security experiments should execute only against the designated controlled sandbox and should use the tests permitted by the experiment configuration.

title: Repeatable findings
content: A security finding should be reproducible using the same controlled test conditions before it is treated as a confirmed result.

title: Finding validation
content: Validation should compare the observed sandbox behavior and evidence against the expected behavior of the selected security test.

title: Evidence consistency
content: Evidence recorded for a finding should correspond to the test that produced it and should support the reported finding.

title: Candidate test safety
content: The adaptive planner should select only tests present in the available sandbox test allowlist and should not invent or execute arbitrary tests.
